script.base: Seattle is a 2.5-point road favorite in a 47.5 game, implied SEA 25.0 / WAS 22.5, so the book expects a competitive night, not a blowout. Base flow: Seattle leans on K.Walker (37 car/186 yds, weeks 5-7) and Z.Charbonnet (33/109) into a Washington run defense allowing 4.69 YPC and 26 runs of 10+, while J.Smith-Njigba (36 tgt/417 yds/449 air) stays the pass engine and A.Barner (13 tgt/131) works the middle. Washington, with T.McLaurin out, tries to stay within a score via Z.Ertz (19 tgt/96) and a split of D.Samuel, J.Lane, C.Moore and J.McNichols, but J.Croskey-Merritt (39 car/119, 3.05 YPC, yards 61 then 33 then 25) is capped by Seattle's 3.40 YPC run defense.
script.flip1: Seattle leads by two scores, runs the clock with Walker/Charbonnet, and JSN/Barner/Kupp yards stall the way a clock-kill script stalls QB/WR production. Washington abandons the run, so Croskey-Merritt's carries die and targets bunch to Ertz, Moore, Lane and McNichols.
script.flip2: It flips into a pass-heavy game (Washington keeps the lead, or Seattle's missing S Julian Love plus 23 allowed 20+ yard passes turn into explosives). Walker finishes closer to his 34-yard game than his 81/86 games, JSN and Washington's air-yard receivers (Lane 147 air, Moore 129 air in the 3-game window) are live, and a Croskey-Merritt under is only safe if Seattle's front still holds the efficiency cap.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both leans lost. Barner finished at 7 again because Seattle led, handed Walker and Charbonnet the ball (they already split 37 and 33 carries), and Washington did not have to blitz, so the seam never opened; the 53 and 71 were the fluky games, not the 7. Croskey-Merritt went over 44.5 because Washington stayed close or ahead, Reed sat, and one explosive run — Seattle allows almost none, which is why a single one flips the leg — plus even a short catch pushed rush+rec over a line that projection math already had near 44. The counter-case is real on both: Barner's form trend is broken, and JCM's expected yards sit on the number. That is why both are leans, flagged, and unpriced, not strong. Walker over 66.5 was considered and dropped: L3 is 62.0 rush yards per game, Charbonnet has 33 carries, newest game was 66, and the WAS 4.69 YPC matchup is already in a fair line. JSN over 123.5 was dropped: primary-target overlap is real, but 123.5 equals the last4 mean and the clock-kill flip kills it. Lane over 13.5 and Moore over 29.5 were the McLaurin sleepers; Lane's newest game is 0, Moore faces a non-bleeding middle/right and a Tunsil question. Samuel under 44.5 was dropped because weeks 6-8 yards (26) and the McLaurin absence point opposite ways.
slip_story: One competitive-game story, not a shootout and not a blowout: Seattle's offense can still use the middle (Barner over 26.5) while Seattle's run defense caps Washington's lead back (Croskey-Merritt rush+rec under 44.5). They win together if the game stays near 25-22 and neither team is forced into a pure run-clock or a pure WAS-leads-and-runs script. Do not add JSN 123.5, a total under, or Walker over to this slip — those need a different script. Two legs only. No TD, no receptions market, one market per player.
